newsitem.title: ITALY: GOLF-STRAIGHT DRIVING OLAZABAL SHARES LEAD IN ITALY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STRAIGHT DRIVING OLAZABAL SHARES LEAD IN ITALY.

text.p: BRESCIA, Italy, May 1 Reuter) - Jose Maria Olazabal enjoyed his best day with the driver since he returned from injury and was rewarded with a share of the lead in the Italian Open on Thursday.
Olazabal's four-under-par 68 left him tied with in-form Argentine Jose Coceres and Sweden's Patrik Sjoland among the early starters at the Gardagolf course.
Four birdies in the last eight holes took Olazabal into first place as he made his bid to add to his Turespana Masters success in the two months' since his comeback.

The key to Olazabal's new challenge was the 'Makser' metal driver produced by his own company. The Spaniard had used a traditional wooden driver before his 18 months enforced layoff because of his career-threatening feet problems.
"I shocked myself today because I drove really, really well for the first time this year," he said. "The driver has been the weakest club in my bag, but not today.

"You need to be long and accurate here, too, because it's a long and demanding course. If they grow the rough and narrow the fairways, it would make a good test for the U.S. Open. It's one of the best courses I've played this year and the European Tour should find us more to test us to the full."

Olazabal revisits his German doctor next week when he takes another break and may decide then whether he will increase his schedule from two to three consecutive events before the British Open in July.
He will play only two successive tournaments before next month's U.S. Open.

"My feet still bother me but they are getting better. I know I need to improve a bit more but I'll decide how many tournaments I play in a row before the British Open when I've got my doctor's opinion."
Coceres, in contention several times this season, carded four birdies while Sjoland cancelled out a double-bogey and bogey with seven birdies.
